the-workspace.title: The workspace
the-workspace.summary: The dashboard, the menu, and how to search from anywhere.
the-workspace.gotcha: An unknown number shows as a dash, not a zero. A dash means the figure could not be loaded — it does not mean nothing happened.

nav-dashboard.title: This is your day
nav-dashboard.body: Pickups and returns for the date you are looking at, what is overdue, and what needs attention. Every tile clicks through to the list behind it.

global-search.title: Find anything from here
global-search.body: Search by customer name, reservation number, plate — or a payment reference, if the agent recorded one. You never need to remember which screen something lives on.

nav-reservations.title: Reservations is where the work happens
nav-reservations.body: Creating, checking out, checking in, payments and extensions all start here.

nav-university.title: Ride University
nav-university.body: Every module you can take, your progress, and the playbooks. You can relaunch this tour from here any time.

find-reservation.title: Find a reservation
find-reservation.summary: By name, number, plate or payment reference.
find-reservation.gotcha: A partial reservation number returning nothing does not mean the reservation does not exist. Search also matches the customer, the plate, and the last four of a card when it was recorded in the payment reference.

reservations-filters.title: Filter to what you need
reservations-filters.body: Today's pickups, today's returns, or everything overdue. A rental counts as overdue the moment its return time passes — not at midnight.

create-reservation.title: Create a reservation
create-reservation.summary: Book a car from scratch, start to finish.
create-reservation.gotcha: Minimum rental is 24 hours unless the vehicle class has an hourly rate configured. And monthly must be chosen on the first step — picking it later means attaching the plan from the reservation page afterwards.

new-reservation-v2.title: Start a new reservation
new-reservation-v2.body: This opens the four-step wizard, with a running quote beside you the whole way.

wizard-step-dates.title: Dates and locations first
wizard-step-dates.body: Pickup and return, and where the car leaves from and comes back to. Choose the rate type here too — daily, or monthly for a long-term rental.

wizard-step-vehicle.title: Pick the class
wizard-step-vehicle.body: The quote updates as you choose, so you can tell the customer the price before you commit to anything.

wizard-step-customer.title: Find or create the customer
wizard-step-customer.body: Search first — most customers are already there. Creating a duplicate splits their rental history in two.

wizard-step-review.title: Review, then confirm
wizard-step-review.body: Now do it for real: complete this booking and the module marks itself finished.

check-out.title: Check a vehicle out
check-out.gotcha: The photo step feels skippable when the lot is busy. It is the only evidence of the vehicle condition at handover — and at check-in the agent sees these exact photos beside the camera.

reservation-checkout.title: Start the handover
reservation-checkout.body: The wizard walks the whole handover in order and will not let you skip what matters.

checkout-terms.title: Terms, signed by the customer
checkout-terms.body: This is the authorization for post-rental charges — fuel, mileage, cleaning, tolls, damage. Without it those charges have no basis.

checkout-inspection-handoff.title: Hand the inspection to a phone
checkout-inspection-handoff.body: This produces a code for the phone that walks the lot. Eight angles get captured there — front, rear, both sides, both seats, dashboard, trunk — and land back on this rental. Ninety seconds now settles an argument weeks later.

check-in.title: Check a vehicle in
check-in.summary: Photos against the checkout, readings, fees, balance.
check-in.gotcha: When the customer returned on time but the check-in is recorded late, the late fee is computed from the moment of the check-in — unless an admin sets the actual return date, a field that only appears for admins past the grace period.

reservation-checkin.title: Start the return
reservation-checkin.body: Same shape as the handover, in reverse.

checkin-photos.title: The checkout photo sits right there
checkin-photos.body: Each angle shows how the car left the lot beside your live camera. Anything new gets noted here, while the customer is still in front of you.

checkin-metrics.title: Mileage, fuel, cleanliness
checkin-metrics.body: The fees compute from these as you type, so you can tell the customer the total before you charge it.

take-payment.title: Take a payment
take-payment.summary: Card, cash or check — and make it findable later.
take-payment.gotcha: The reference field is what makes a payment findable months later. Fill it with the receipt or auth number and the card last four — without it, answering "who paid with the card ending 1234?" means opening reservations one at a time.

reservation-payments.title: Open payments
reservation-payments.body: Everything charged and collected on this rental, in one place.

payment-reference.title: Always fill the reference
payment-reference.body: Receipt or auth number, plus the card last four. This is the single habit that makes the money searchable.

additional-drivers.title: Add an additional driver
additional-drivers.summary: Put a second driver on the agreement, license and all.
additional-drivers.gotcha: Confirm additional drivers BEFORE releasing the vehicle — a driver who is not on the agreement is not covered, and the configured fee does not charge itself after closeout.

reservation-additional-drivers.title: Open Additional Drivers
reservation-additional-drivers.body: Every extra driver lives inside the reservation itself. This button opens the driver roster for the rental you have open.

additional-driver-form.title: Add the driver, license and all
additional-driver-form.body: Name, address, date of birth, license number — and a photo of the license. Every field matters: this is who is covered behind the wheel. Add Driver puts them on the list below.

additional-drivers-save.title: Save before you hand over the keys
additional-drivers-save.body: Nobody on the list counts until you save. Saving puts the roster on the reservation and returns you to it — do this before the vehicle leaves, never after.

overdue-returns.title: Chase an overdue return
overdue-returns.summary: Find them, and find the car.
overdue-returns.gotcha: A car sitting on one of your own lots raises no alert. That is a missed check-in, not a missing car — two different problems with two different fixes.

kpi-overdue.title: Overdue, at a glance
kpi-overdue.body: Click through to the list. A rental is overdue the moment its return time passes.

overdue-alerts.title: Where the car actually is
overdue-alerts.body: With GPS connected, anything overdue and outside every one of your branches raises an alert here, with the distance and a map link. Nothing showing means nothing is missing.

availability.title: Check availability
availability.summary: What is free, what is out, what is down.
availability.gotcha: If you have switched your view to one location, exports follow that view. Switch back to all locations before exporting a fleet-wide roster.

nav-reports.title: Availability by class
nav-reports.body: Available, reserved, on rent, in maintenance — per vehicle class, right now.

report-export.title: Export the roster
report-export.body: PDF or Excel, and both now carry every vehicle with its status, not just the totals.

users-and-locations.title: Add a user and scope them
users-and-locations.summary: Roles, and which branches they can see.
users-and-locations.gotcha: A location-scoped agent sees only their own branches everywhere — including which locations they can book from. If an agent cannot create a reservation, check their location scope first.

nav-people.title: People
nav-people.body: Everyone with access, and what they can reach.

view-location-switcher.title: Viewing as one branch
view-location-switcher.body: Anyone with more than one location gets this switcher. It changes what they see everywhere — including what their exports contain.

person-type.title: Pick what kind of person this is
person-type.body: Employee, admin, host or virtual agent. The choice sets their starting permissions, so it is the first thing to get right — changing it later means re-checking everything below it.

person-access-role.title: Then their access role
person-access-role.body: AGENT works the counter. OPS adds the operational screens. ADMIN can change settings and manage people. When in doubt give less: raising someone later is one click, undoing what they changed is an audit.

person-locations.title: Scope them to their branch
person-locations.body: Check the locations this person works at. Leaving every box UNCHECKED is not "no access" — it means they see ALL locations. That is the most common mistake on this screen.

incoming-bookings.title: Bookings arriving on their own
incoming-bookings.summary: Franchise and broker feeds, and the review tray.
incoming-bookings.gotcha: A booking in the review tray is not an error. It is the system refusing to guess — usually a customer it could not match with confidence.

nav-settings.title: Integrations
nav-settings.body: Each connected franchise or broker pulls reservations in on a schedule, matched to customers and checked for duplicates before anyone sees them.

pending-imports.title: The review tray
pending-imports.body: Anything that did not match cleanly waits here with what the system found, for a person to decide. It hides itself when there is nothing waiting — an empty screen is good news.

market-pricing.title: Price against the market
market-pricing.summary: What competitors charge, beside what you charge.
market-pricing.gotcha: Prices update nightly, not live. And the day filters are how far ahead the pickup is — the booking window — not how long the rental lasts.

nav-market.title: The market, by class
nav-market.body: Competitor offers collected nightly across the major booking sites, mapped to the same vehicle classes your fleet uses.

market-strategy.title: Where the strategy pays off
market-strategy.body: You choose where to sit — second cheapest, for instance — and how far a price may move on its own. Anything bigger lands in this inbox for you to approve.

shuttle-dispatch.title: Run the shuttle console
shuttle-dispatch.summary: The live map, who is driving, and the zones that raise alerts.
shuttle-dispatch.gotcha: A driver link is a shift, not a person. Minting a second link for the same driver does not move them — it leaves two live shifts, and the map shows the bus twice. Revoke the old one when a shift changes hands.

shuttle-console.title: The console, in three tabs
shuttle-console.body: The live map shows every shuttle transmitting right now, filtered to the location you pick. Positions refresh on their own roughly every twelve seconds — you never need to reload the page.

shuttle-drivers-tab.title: Who is driving, right now
shuttle-drivers-tab.body: Driver shifts are handed out as links, not logins: mint one, the driver opens it on their phone, and their position starts feeding the map customers watch. Revoke it and the feed stops immediately.

shuttle-zones-tab.title: Zones are what make alerts mean something
shuttle-zones-tab.body: A zone is the area a shuttle is supposed to stay inside. Draw them once and the system tells you when a bus leaves its route or stops moving — instead of you watching a map all day.

shuttle-tracker.title: The live shuttle tracker
shuttle-tracker.summary: Customers watch the shuttle move on a live map and request it with one tap.
shuttle-tracker.gotcha: Never screenshot or forward a tracker link — each one is personal to a single reservation and expires when the rental ends. The next customer gets their own automatically, by email and SMS. A shared link that suddenly dies at the curb is worse than no link.

shuttle-queue.title: Every request lands here
shuttle-queue.body: Customers picking up at a tracker-enabled location get a personal, expiring link by email and SMS. They watch the shuttle move on a live map, see exactly where to stand, and one tap requests the pickup — it appears on this screen for the floor team. Repeat taps and repeat calls fold into the same request: one anxious customer is one bus, not three.

kiosk-cant-scan.title: The guest cannot scan their license
kiosk-cant-scan.summary: From “I can’t — get help” to verifying the ID yourself with your PIN.
kiosk-cant-scan.gotcha: Your PIN opens a ten-minute window — it does not bend a rule. Age and license validity run exactly as they do for a scan; the name check is the one thing it skips, because you are holding the physical license in front of the guest and that is what your PIN certifies. If the real date of birth fails, the kiosk is telling the truth: “End assist” and let the counter decide.

kiosk-fig-scan-trouble.title: Two failed scans
kiosk-fig-scan-trouble.body: The guest is on “Scan your driver’s license”, barcode side up, and the reader is not catching it. Glare, a worn card, a laminated copy — it happens. Before anyone is called, the screen already offers two ways around it.

callouts.0: “Upload barcode photo” — a still photo is often readable when the live camera is not.
callouts.1: “Take a photo instead” reads the FRONT of the license instead, then asks the guest to confirm what it read.

kiosk-fig-escalated.title: They ask for a person
kiosk-fig-escalated.body: The guest taps “I can't do this — get help”. The kiosk switches to “A team member is on the way” and notifies the counter. Nothing is lost: the reservation, the step, everything they entered stays in the session.

callouts.0: If they tap 🎧 Help instead, the help chat opens and a Valet agent takes over remotely — that is its own module.
callouts.1: The small “Staff assist” button at the bottom is your door in.

kiosk-fig-staff-pin.title: Unlock with your PIN
kiosk-fig-staff-pin.body: Tap “Staff assist”, pick your name and enter your PIN on the keypad. “Unlock” opens a ten-minute grant in your name — the chip shows who and how long, and it closes on its own.

callouts.0: Your name greyed out means you have no PIN yet — set one in your profile first.
callouts.1: Wrong PINs, wrong codes and failed lookups all feed one counter for this kiosk — the screen says how many attempts are left. At zero it locks for fifteen minutes.
callouts.2: “Cancel — back to guest” closes the panel without a grant.

kiosk-fig-staff-manual-id.title: Type the license in, photograph both sides
kiosk-fig-staff-manual-id.body: Fill in first name, last name, date of birth and expiry exactly as printed. Then “Capture” or “Upload” the FRONT and the BACK of the physical license — both are required, and they are stored with the rental.

callouts.0: The photos are the evidence that a person saw the card. Without both, “Verify & continue” stays off.

kiosk-fig-staff-verify.title: Verify and continue — two rules still run
kiosk-fig-staff-verify.body: Two checks, not three: the age requirement and a license valid through the return date. The name check is deliberately NOT run here — you are holding the physical license in front of the guest, and that is exactly what your PIN certifies. A typo can be corrected and verified again. A real failure cannot be talked past.

callouts.0: A red mark here is the kiosk doing its job — check the fields for a typo first.
callouts.1: “Verify & continue” runs the two checks again with what you typed.
callouts.2: “End assist” closes without verifying; the rental is then the counter’s call.

kiosk-fig-guest-notice-done.title: What the guest sees now
kiosk-fig-guest-notice-done.body: “ID verified by staff” hands control back with “Continue as guest”. From then on a green notice reads “Your ID was confirmed by Ana Rivera from our team.” — the name is your real user account, and it stays on screen for the rest of the check-in.

callouts.0: The record keeps who, when, and that it was in person — distinct from a remote override.

kiosk-check-cant-scan.title: Quick check
kiosk-check-cant-scan.body: One question before this module closes.

check.question: You typed the license in and the kiosk says the guest does not meet the minimum age. What do you do?

A.text: Re-enter a “corrected” date of birth so it passes
A.why: That is falsifying a rental record under your own PIN. The date of birth on the license is the date of birth.

B.text: Check for a typo; if the date is real, end the assistance and let the counter decide
B.why: Nothing skips the rules — not your PIN, not a remote agent. A real failure is the kiosk doing its job.

C.text: Ask Valet to approve it remotely
C.why: Remote agents run the very same checks. There is no override for age or validity anywhere in the system.

kiosk-name-mismatch.title: The name on the license does not match
kiosk-name-mismatch.summary: The guest’s own way out (a 6-digit code) and yours (certifying the license).
kiosk-name-mismatch.gotcha: When you confirm the name you are certifying, under your own account, that you looked at the physical license and it belongs to this person. When the guest can prove it themselves with the code, let them — it leaves the cleaner trail.

kiosk-fig-name-mismatch.title: The license read fine — the name did not match
kiosk-fig-name-mismatch.body: Age and validity pass; only the name check is red. Common causes: a maiden name, a second surname, a booking made by a spouse. The kiosk does not fail the guest here — it offers two ways to prove the reservation is theirs.

callouts.0: Two green, one red: this is a NAME problem, not an ID problem.
callouts.1: “Send my code” — the guest proves it themselves (next step).
callouts.2: “Connect me to a team member” — a person confirms it, in person or from Valet.

kiosk-fig-name-code.title: The guest proves it with a code
kiosk-fig-name-code.body: A 6-digit code goes to the email or phone ON THE RESERVATION — never to a number the guest types now. Entering it updates the reservation to the license name and the check-in continues. It expires in ten minutes.

callouts.0: “Confirm code” — wrong codes count against the kiosk’s shared attempt counter; the screen says how many are left before it locks.
callouts.1: “Resend code” has a cooldown so the inbox is not flooded.

kiosk-fig-staff-name-confirm.title: Or you confirm it, in person
kiosk-fig-staff-name-confirm.body: Unlock with your PIN as usual. Instead of the full form the kiosk shows both names side by side. “I verified this license matches the guest” records that YOU looked at the card and vouched — the rental carries your name on that decision.

callouts.0: License name versus reservation name, exactly as each system has them.
callouts.1: This button is a certification, not a shortcut. If you did not see the card, do not press it.

kiosk-check-name-mismatch.title: Quick check
kiosk-check-name-mismatch.body: One question before this module closes.

check.question: The guest says the reservation was made by her husband, who is not here. The license is hers. What is the right path?

A.text: Press “I verified this license matches the guest” — it is her license
A.why: Her license is real, but the reservation is not in her name. Certifying the name does not put a driver on someone else’s booking.

B.text: Have the guest use “Send my code” — the code goes to the contact on the reservation
B.why: If the husband shares the code, the booking updates to her name with his consent on record. If he cannot, the counter decides the rental.

C.text: Tell her to start over and search by her own name
C.why: There is no reservation under her name to find. Starting over only erases what she entered.

kiosk-valet-help.title: The guest asks for help by chat and Valet takes it
kiosk-valet-help.summary: What the guest sees, what a remote agent can and cannot do, and why the keys are yours to hand over.
kiosk-valet-help.gotcha: When Valet finishes, the guest still has to walk to you for the key. The green notice on their screen is your cue — have it ready.

kiosk-fig-help-chat.title: 🎧 Help opens a chat with a Valet agent
kiosk-fig-help-chat.body: The guest can tap Help on any screen. A Valet agent sees which step they are on and what has been verified — never the license photos, never card details. The chat sits over the check-in without ending it.

callouts.0: Help is always in the corner. It never ends the session.
callouts.1: Closing the chat asks “End help chat?” — the check-in stays where it was.

kiosk-fig-guest-notice-now.title: While the agent works, the guest is told
kiosk-fig-guest-notice-now.body: A violet notice reads “Ana Rivera from our team is helping you with this check-in right now.” for as long as the agent holds a grant (ten minutes, then it closes by itself). The name is the REAL user account behind the action — never a name the console typed. A service account shows “Someone from our team is helping you with this check-in right now.”.

callouts.0: Violet = happening now. It turns green (“your ID was confirmed… remotely”) once the override is applied.
callouts.1: “✓ Your agent updated your check-in” confirms an action landed.
callouts.2: Attempts to skip signing or paying from the chat are refused on screen.

kiosk-fig-remote-limits.title: What a remote agent can — and cannot — do
kiosk-fig-remote-limits.body: Can: unlock the session, enter the license by hand from the photos already on file, confirm the name. Cannot: skip verification, sign, pay — and cannot open the car. The remote unlock goes to a lockbox that does not exist yet, so the agent tells the guest to collect the keys at the front desk.

callouts.0: Everything here runs the same rules as the kiosk itself.
callouts.1: Signature and payment are the guest’s alone, at the kiosk.
callouts.2: Keys: “Please see a team member at the counter to pick up your keys.” — that is you.

kiosk-check-valet-keys.title: Quick check
kiosk-check-valet-keys.body: One question before this module closes.

check.question: The guest has signed, and a Valet agent confirmed their identity remotely. Who hands over the key?

A.why: There is no remote unlock. That path leads to a lockbox the location does not have yet.

B.text: The front desk — the agent tells the guest to come collect it
B.why: Remote help ends at the screen. The car changes hands at the counter, with you.

C.text: The kiosk prints a pickup code
C.why: The kiosk prints nothing. The “All set” screen says “Please see a team member at the counter to pick up your keys.”.

kiosk-payment.title: The payment fails or the kiosk does not move on
kiosk-payment.summary: The link and QR, and what to do when the screen does not advance.
kiosk-payment.gotcha: Never charge by hand what the kiosk is charging. A “stuck” screen is usually a payment that landed a few seconds ago — look in Reservations → Payments before touching the terminal. And if two payments ever land (an old QR left open on the phone), refund the extra one; never re-charge.

kiosk-fig-pay-qr.title: One link, one QR, and the kiosk waits
kiosk-fig-pay-qr.body: “Show payment code” creates ONE payment link to the tenant’s hosted payment page and shows it as a QR. The guest scans it and pays on their phone. The kiosk shows “Waiting for payment…” and moves to the signature by itself the moment the server confirms. Pressing “Show payment code” again with the same total shows the SAME link.

callouts.0: The QR is a link to the payment page — the kiosk never sees the card.
callouts.1: “Waiting for payment…” polls every few seconds. Give it ten to fifteen. A declined card is retried by the guest on their phone, from this same QR.
callouts.2: What is charged today versus the refundable hold on the card.

kiosk-fig-pay-failed.title: If the total changes
kiosk-fig-pay-failed.body: “Change protection & extras” goes back to extras. A new total mints a NEW link and QR; the old one leaves the kiosk screen but is STILL payable if the guest left it open on their phone — there is no way to cancel it at the gateway. Have the guest close the old payment page before scanning the new code. If two payments land, both show under Reservations → Payments: refund the extra one, never re-charge.

callouts.0: “Try again” belongs to the sandbox/failed screen — it is not a link action. Same-total reuse comes from pressing “Show payment code” again.
callouts.1: “Change protection & extras” — a new total means a new link; the old one is off the screen, not dead.

kiosk-check-payment.title: Quick check
kiosk-check-payment.body: One question before this module closes.

check.question: The guest says they paid on their phone, but the kiosk still shows “Waiting for payment…”. What do you do?

A.text: Charge them on the counter terminal so they can move on
A.why: That is the double charge. The kiosk’s payment may have landed seconds ago — the screen just has not polled yet.

B.text: Wait ten to fifteen seconds, then check Reservations → Payments
B.why: If the payment is there, the kiosk will catch up. If it is not, the guest retries on their phone from the same QR — or you press “Show payment code” again, which shows the same link for the same total.

C.text: Tap “Start over” and begin the check-in again
C.why: That erases the session. The payment, if it landed, stays attached to the reservation — but the guest redoes everything.

kiosk-brakes.title: “Still there?”, “Not my reservation”, and a locked kiosk
kiosk-brakes.summary: The three ways the kiosk stops itself: inactivity, a wrong match, and fifteen minutes of lockout.
kiosk-brakes.gotcha: A locked kiosk is not broken. An admin clears it on the spot by issuing a new pairing code (Ride Fleet → Kiosks); with no admin at hand, finish the guest at the counter — in fifteen minutes it is back by itself. Restarting the iPad changes nothing: the lock lives on the server.

kiosk-fig-idle.title: “Are you still there?” — the privacy reset
kiosk-fig-idle.body: After a pause with no touch, the kiosk asks. “I'm still here — continue” keeps everything. If nobody answers, the countdown reaches zero and the session resets, clearing what was entered — a stranger walking up must never see the last guest’s reservation.

callouts.0: “I'm still here — continue” keeps every field filled so far.
callouts.1: “Start over” clears it all on purpose — there is no undo.

kiosk-fig-not-mine.title: “This isn't my reservation”
kiosk-fig-not-mine.body: The summary shows driver, dates and class before anything else happens. If it is the wrong one, “This isn't my reservation” goes back to the search without spending an attempt. Lookups by number have a limited number of tries — the search screen says how many are left — and once spent, the kiosk pauses searches for a few minutes.

callouts.0: “That's me — continue” is the guest confirming the match.
callouts.1: “This isn't my reservation” is free — it does not count as a failed attempt.

kiosk-fig-locked.title: Locked for fifteen minutes
kiosk-fig-locked.body: Too many wrong PINs, wrong codes or failed lookups, and the kiosk pauses staff unlock and searches. It is protecting the guest data on it. Two ways out: an admin issues a new pairing code from Ride Fleet → Kiosks and the lock clears immediately — or you wait it out and finish the guest at the counter.

callouts.0: There is no timer on screen — the lock simply lifts by itself after fifteen minutes.
callouts.1: The screen itself says it: an admin can issue a new pairing code to clear it right away.

kiosk-check-locked.title: Quick check
kiosk-check-locked.body: One question before this module closes.

check.question: The kiosk shows “This kiosk is temporarily locked” after a colleague ran its attempt counter down with wrong PINs. A guest is waiting and no admin is around. What do you do?

A.text: Keep trying PINs until one works
A.why: While locked, every attempt is refused before it is even counted — it does nothing except keep the guest standing there.

B.text: Finish the guest at the counter; the kiosk unlocks itself in fifteen minutes — or an admin clears it now with a new pairing code
B.why: The lockout is protection, not a fault. The counter does everything the kiosk does, and Ride Fleet → Kiosks → new pairing code clears it instantly when an admin is available.

C.why: The lock lives on the server, not the tablet. A restart changes nothing and loses the guest’s session.

kiosk-done-keys.title: They signed: keys, contract and the photo walk-around
kiosk-done-keys.summary: The “All set!” screen — where the key is, what arrived by email, and the inspection link.
kiosk-done-keys.gotcha: The screen resets itself after a 30-second countdown. If the guest wants a printed contract, print it from the reservation — the kiosk cannot.

kiosk-fig-done.title: “All set!” — three things to point at
kiosk-fig-done.body: Keys: “Please see a team member at the counter to pick up your keys.” Contract and receipt: already in their email. Before leaving: a QR (or emailed link) to photo-document the car’s condition — the same inspection the counter would do, done by the guest on their phone.

callouts.0: Keys are handed by you, at the counter — unless your location is set to Lockbox in Ride Fleet → Kiosks, in which case the screen sends the guest to the lockbox instead.
callouts.1: Contract and receipt went to the email on the reservation.
callouts.2: The inspection link is how damage disputes are settled later — encourage it.

kiosk-check-done.title: Quick check
kiosk-check-done.body: One question before this module closes.

check.question: The guest at “All set!” asks for a printed copy of the contract. What do you do?

A.text: Tap the screen before it resets and print from the kiosk
A.why: The kiosk has no printer and no print button. The “All set!” screen only resets.

B.text: Print it from the reservation on your own screen
B.why: Every signed agreement is on the reservation. The kiosk already emailed it; you can print it.

C.why: It is in their email, but a printed copy is a normal request — and you can fulfil it in seconds.

kiosk-grant-valet.title: Give Valet access to the kiosk
kiosk-grant-valet.summary: People → the Valet service account → the Kiosk module. Without it, Valet cannot see kiosk sessions.
kiosk-grant-valet.gotcha: Two switches, not one: the Kiosk module must be on for the company (Settings) AND ticked on the service account. Access is cached per user for a few minutes, so a change may take a moment to reach Valet.

person-module-kiosk.title: Tick “Kiosk” on the Valet service account
person-module-kiosk.body: Open the Valet service account in People, scroll to User Module Access, tick Kiosk and save. This is what lets a Valet agent see where a guest is stuck and help from the console. Every change here is recorded with your name.

kiosk-check-grant.title: Quick check
kiosk-check-grant.body: One question before this module closes.

check.question: Valet reports “we cannot see the kiosk sessions” for a new location. Kiosk is ticked on the service account. What else can it be?

A.text: The Kiosk module is off for the company in Settings — the user tick does nothing on its own
A.why: Tenant module settings apply on top of per-user access. Both must be on.

B.text: Valet needs a PIN like an employee
B.why: PINs are for in-person unlock at the kiosk. Remote access is the service account plus the module.

C.text: Each kiosk must be paired to Valet individually
C.why: Pairing binds an iPad to the location. Valet reads sessions through the module, not through pairing.

kiosk.title: What does every button do?
kiosk.summary: Every button on the kiosk and on the staff panel, by screen.

name.title: Name does not match (guest’s own way out)

entries.help: Opens the help chat with a Valet agent. It never ends the session or loses a step.
entries.back: One step back without losing what was entered. On the payment screen it also discards the QR code being shown.
entries.start-over: Clears EVERYTHING the guest entered and returns to the welcome screen. There is no undo.
entries.still-here: Answers “Still there?”. If nobody taps, the session resets on its own for privacy.
entries.get-help: Shown after a generic error: escalate to a team member, or repeat the action that failed.
entries.walkup: Walk-up rentals. Today it shows “coming very soon” and sends the guest to the counter.
entries.scan-qr: The QR from the confirmation email. Today it shows “coming soon” — type the confirmation number instead.
entries.find: Looks up by confirmation number. Attempts are limited; once spent, the kiosk pauses lookups for a few minutes.
entries.by-name: Last name plus the pickup day, or the phone number on file. If several match, the kiosk asks for one more detail.
entries.thats-me: Confirms the reservation found — or goes back to search without spending an attempt.
entries.scan: Reads the PDF417 barcode on the BACK and fills in name, license number, date of birth and expiry. “Stop scanning” turns the camera off.
entries.upload-barcode: A still photo of the barcode — often readable when the live camera is not.
entries.photo: Reads the FRONT of the license from a photo, then shows “Is this correct?” with what it read. “Retake” starts over.
entries.confirm-read: The guest confirms the fields read from the photo are theirs.
entries.cant-scan: Escalates: “A team member is on the way” — the counter is notified. Nothing escalates by itself; the guest (or you) presses it.
entries.connect: Shown when verification fails: open the chat with Valet, or scan again.
entries.entry: Your door into the panel, from the escalation screen. Employees with a PIN only.
entries.unlock: Name + PIN opens a TEN-MINUTE grant in your name (“Ana — 9:58 left”). Wrong PINs share one attempt counter with lookups and codes; at zero the kiosk locks for fifteen minutes.
entries.cancel: Closes the panel without a grant; the guest is exactly where they were.
entries.capture: Photos of the FRONT and BACK of the physical license. Both are required.
entries.verify: Runs two real rules — age and license validity. The name check is deliberately skipped here (you are holding the license). YOUR PIN DOES NOT SKIP THE OTHER TWO.
entries.name-confirm: You certify the name matches after checking the physical license. Recorded under your name.
entries.continue-guest: Hands control back to the guest — or closes without verifying, and the counter decides the rental.
entries.send-code: Sends a 6-digit code to the email or phone ON THE RESERVATION. Expires in 10 minutes.
entries.confirm-code: Validates the code and updates the reservation to the license name. Resend has a cooldown; attempts are limited.
entries.not-eligible: No button here: the correction is done by staff with “I verified this license belongs to the guest”.
entries.close-chat: Ends the conversation, with a confirmation. The check-in is not lost.
entries.agent-can: The agent can UNLOCK, ENTER THE ID BY HAND (from the photos already on file) and CONFIRM THE NAME. The guest sees this toast and the violet/green notice.
entries.agent-cannot: The agent cannot skip verification, sign or pay — and cannot open the car. Keys are handed at the front desk.
entries.add-extras: Adds what is ticked to the total (prices are for the rental’s days), or continues without extras. Every option includes the deposit.
entries.selfie: Identity selfie. “Upload a photo” when there is no camera.
entries.show-qr: Creates ONE payment link to the tenant’s hosted payment page and shows its QR. The guest pays on their phone; the kiosk shows “Waiting for payment…” and advances by itself.
entries.retry: Only on the sandbox/failed screen; it is not a link action. A real declined card is retried by the guest on their phone from the same QR. Pressing “Show payment code” again shows the same link for the same total.
entries.change-extras: Back to extras. A new total mints a NEW link; the previous one leaves the screen but stays payable if the guest left it open on their phone — have them close it. Two payments landing = refund the extra, never re-charge.

checkinWizard.selfReturnApplied: Customer marked the return at {{time}} — the late fee is computed up to that hour, not the check-in hour.
checkinWizard.selfReturnLater: Customer marked the return at {{time}} (after the return time of this close — it does not change the fee).
checkinWizard.selfReturnVoided: A customer return mark exists but was voided by an admin — it is not used.
checkinWizard.mileagePrefilled: Pre-filled with the vehicle's last known mileage — edit it if the odometer reads different.
checkinWizard.mileageWarning: Entered mileage ({{entered}} mi) is below the check-out reading ({{baseline}} mi). Double-check the odometer — continue only if this is a correction or the odometer was swapped.
checkinWizard.damageHint: Record damage found at return without leaving the check-in. It logs the damage, adds the charge to this contract and starts the incident draft.
checkinWizard.damageRecorded: Damage report recorded — the charge was added to this contract.

checkinAudit.title: Check-in Audit
checkinAudit.sub: Post-return review — rules audit on every close
checkinAudit.damageLaneClear: No possible-damage flags right now — the photo sweep runs a few minutes after each close.
checkinAudit.t2SkippedBudget: Skipped — the daily photo-AI budget was reached before this close.
checkinAudit.t2SkippedNoPhotos: Skipped — no angle has a photo on both the checkout and check-in side.
checkinAudit.t2Failed: The photo analysis failed — the check-in itself is unaffected.
checkinAudit.t2Pending: Queued for the photo sweep — it runs a few minutes after each close.
checkinAudit.damageLaneEmpty: Photo AI is not enabled — this lane fills when the photo tier (T2) ships. Rules findings live in Entry errors and Mileage / fuel.
checkinAudit.railNote: A check-in is never held by the audit. Flags appear here after the close.
checkinAudit.t2Placeholder: Photo AI is not enabled. When the photo tier ships (opt-in per tenant, tenant key), checkout and check-in photos of each angle are compared here and possible new damage lands in the queue — a person always confirms; nothing is ever charged automatically.

pair.clean: No new marks suspected on this angle.

verdict.title: Possible new damage
verdict.knownMatched: The model also matched documented baseline damage in this view — shown for context, never hidden.
verdict.disclaimer: AI suggestion — a staff member confirms. The highlighted box is a pointer, not a measurement, and nothing is ever charged automatically.

rows.impossibleFail: in < out — one entry is wrong

dismiss.title: Dismiss this flag
dismiss.notIssueSub: The check misread the situation. Logged as reviewed — nothing else happens.
dismiss.preexistingSub: Adds it to this vehicle's damage baseline so it is never flagged again — and never charged to a customer.
dismiss.preexistingT2: Applies to photo-AI damage findings — awaits the photo tier (T2). Rules findings are numbers, not marks.

handoff.sub: Opens the Report Damage wizard with the evidence already loaded — photos, view and description pre-filled; the agent enters the estimate and who pays.
handoff.baselined: Added to the vehicle's damage baseline · {{name}}

damageBaseline.title: Damage baseline
damageBaseline.sub: Documented marks on this vehicle — the known-damage baseline. Entries leave the diagram by being repaired (photo required), by a completed repair order, or by clear-with-reason; everything stays in the history below.
damageBaseline.none: No damage on record for this vehicle.
damageBaseline.sendRoConfirm: Group this damage into a new repair order? Completing the RO marks it repaired.
damageBaseline.clearPrompt: Clear WITHOUT a repair — why? (e.g. "was dirt", "double entry"). This is recorded in the audit log.
damageBaseline.cleared: Entry cleared — kept in history with the reason

disclosure.title: Documented marks on this vehicle
disclosure.sub: Point these out to the customer during the walkthrough — they are on record and are NOT the customer’s responsibility.

seed.title: Seed from history
seed.sub: Uses what the system already stores about this vehicle — acknowledged damage reports, inspection damage notes and damage incidents. Everything is created as a PROPOSAL you review; nothing lands on the baseline without your approval.
seed.capped: Capped at {{cap}} per run ({{total}} found) — run again for the rest.
seed.nothing: Nothing new to seed — history is either empty or already reflected on the baseline.
seed.done: Seeded {{n}} proposals from history — review them below
seed.doneCapped: Seeded {{n}} proposals — capped ({{total}} candidates found); run again for the rest
seed.proposedTitle: Proposed from history ({{n}}) — approve or discard
seed.proposedSub: Seeded entries are drafts: pick the correct view and approve to put them on the baseline, or discard. Approved dots land at the diagram center — move the customer conversation, not the dot.

locationClauses.title: Contract clauses
locationClauses.loadFailed: Could not load this location’s clauses.
locationClauses.scopeNote: These are the acknowledgements a renter reads and initials at THIS location only. Other locations keep their own wording. Text saved here is what the renter signs and what is re-printed inside the signed agreement.
locationClauses.storageBrokenTitle: The stored clause overrides for this location are not readable.
locationClauses.storageBrokenBody: Every renter here is currently signing the standard text. The boxes below show the standard text; saving will replace the unreadable value.
locationClauses.strandedKeys_one: The stored value contains {{count}} entry that matches no clause and has never taken effect: {{keys}}. Saving will remove it.
locationClauses.strandedKeys_other: The stored value contains {{count}} entries that match no clause and have never taken effect: {{keys}}. Saving will remove them.
locationClauses.terminalBlockedTitle: Check-outs at this location will be signed on the renter’s phone, not the counter terminal.
locationClauses.terminalBlockedBody: The counter terminal can display at most {{max}} characters per clause and refuses rather than cutting a clause in half. Over the limit: {{keys}}.
locationClauses.terminalOkBody: Every clause fits the counter terminal’s {{max}}-character limit, so check-outs here can be signed on the terminal.
locationClauses.whenDeclined: Only when the renter declines counter insurance
locationClauses.whenDamage: Only in the Report Damage wizard — never on the counter terminal
locationClauses.consequenceNear: {{left}} characters left before the terminal refuses this clause and check-outs move to the phone.
locationClauses.consequenceOver: Over {{max}}. The counter terminal will refuse this clause, so check-outs here move to the renter’s phone. You can still save it.
locationClauses.consequenceDamage: Signed on a tablet in the damage wizard — no length limit applies.
locationClauses.canonicalOver: The standard wording for this clause is {{n}} characters — longer than the terminal can show. Until this location replaces it with a shorter text, any check-out that includes this clause is signed on the renter’s phone.
locationClauses.previewRefused: The terminal never shows this clause. The check-out stops before the device is touched and the agent is sent to the phone flow — the clause is not cut short.
locationClauses.separateSave: Clauses save on their own — “Save Location Settings” below does not carry them.

partnerships.title: Partnerships
partnerships.subtitle: Alliance programs with their own prices, terms and hosted page
partnerships.emptyBody: Create your first alliance: upload the partner's logo, set its prices and terms, and publish a page with a QR for their counter.
partnerships.createCodeHelp: Typed by staff in New Reservation and by customers on the site. Auto-generated if empty.
partnerships.confirmPauseBody: The page goes offline immediately and printed QR codes will show "program not available". Existing reservations are not touched. You can resume any time.
partnerships.confirmPublishBody: Publish {{name}}? The hosted page and the program prices go live for customers who open the link or scan the QR.
partnerships.domainHelp: Where partner pages live. Leave empty to serve them from Ride Fleet Manager.
partnerships.domainFallback: Without a domain, pages are served at {{url}}/<slug>

missing.name: name
missing.vehicleMode: preferred type is only for insurers

profile.name: Partner name
profile.validHelp: When it ends, the page and printed QRs show "program not available".
profile.logoHelp: PNG / JPEG / WebP ≤ 2 MB, transparent background. Shown at 38 px on a white plate; without a logo the name is used.
profile.showContact: Show the company's full contact block (locations, phones, email, hours)
profile.showTerms: Link the company's general terms next to the program terms
profile.customerSees: What the customer sees on the page

terms.title: Program terms
terms.help: The alliance's own conditions. Shown as "Program terms" next to the company's general terms. HTML (paragraphs, lists, links) is sanitized on save.
terms.enEmpty: The English page will fall back to the Spanish text.
terms.version: Version {{n}} — customers accept the version live when they book.
terms.partnerNote: Partner note (e.g. "present your insured card at the counter")

pricing.modeRateHelp: Creates the rate PARTNER-<slug> (purpose PARTNER: invisible to the public site and to the counter). Price per class; date overrides in Rates if needed.
pricing.modeDiscountHelp: A fixed % off what the site quotes today, applied as an effective daily rate. The checkout shows the strike-through.
pricing.gridTitle: Price per class · compared with the online rate
pricing.failClosed: A class without a partner price does not appear on the page (fail-closed, like the public site). It is never quoted at another class's price. Both columns are BASE prices (before taxes and fees). Revenue pricing never touches partner books.
pricing.noOnline: No online rate found for this location — the online column stays empty.

vehicles.switch: Show vehicles from inventory on the page
vehicles.switchOn: ON: the customer sees classes with photo and program price and chooses (only classes with a partner price).
vehicles.switchOff: OFF: no inventory is shown; what happens next depends on the partner type.
vehicles.preferredTitle: The customer picks the vehicle type they prefer
vehicles.preferredHelp: A list of types (no photos or units); they mark a preference and accept the disclosure. The reservation is created with that type as a PREFERENCE, no car; the counter assigns per coverage and availability.
vehicles.assignHelp: The customer picks nothing; the reservation is created with the default class.
vehicles.assignInsurerHelp: Available for partners that are not insurers.
vehicles.defaultTypeHelp: Required to publish in this mode.
vehicles.allowedTypesShow: Classes to show (empty = every class with a partner price)
vehicles.disclosure: Coverage disclosure (the customer reads and accepts it) · ES
vehicles.disclosureHelp: Default text, editable. The customer must tick "I understand" before continuing; the acceptance and the disclosure version are stored on the reservation.
vehicles.pricingConfirm: Per coverage · confirmed at pickup (no number, no online payment)
vehicles.pricingType: Program price of the preferred type
vehicles.askPolicy: Ask for policy / claim number (optional field)
vehicles.noPriced: No class has a partner price yet — go to Pricing.
vehicles.typesFailClosed: Only classes with a partner price are shown to the customer.

services.title: Program services
services.help: Company services can be turned on/off and get a program price; a "partner-only" service never appears on the public site, kiosk or counter. "Mandatory" is added by the server at checkout.

hosted.urlHelp: Base domain in Hosted domain settings. Without one, Ride Fleet Manager serves the page.
hosted.qrHelp: Points to the public URL + utm_source=qr. Exported at 1024 px with a quiet zone.
hosted.noReservations: No reservations attributed to this program yet.

partnerships.urlOnPublish: URL is generated when you publish
